practice.title: Implement Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
practice.statementHtml: The all-pairs exercise reads graph (0–3), then start (0–5). Use the directed Floyd-Warshall scenarios; start selects only the route to reconstruct after the matrix is complete. Print the six-by-six distance matrix with spaces, one row per line, using -1 for INF. Then print a path from start to F, or no path to F. For this Floyd-Warshall Algorithm solution, the first output line is Enter graph (0-3) and start (0-5):. Vertex indices are A=0 through F=5.
hints: সব জোড়ার আপডেট একই k নিয়ে শেষ করো।

practice.title: Count finite ordered routes
practice.statementHtml: The ordered-pair statistics program takes one graph number, from 0 to 3, for the directed distance table. Print the final six-row matrix with -1 for INF. Then count reachable ordered pairs i,j with i different from j, and the largest finite distance among those pairs. Print reachable pairs followed by the count, then largest distance followed by the maximum. Use zero for the maximum when no distinct pair is reachable. Begin the Count finite ordered routes output with Enter graph (0-3):. Vertex indices are A=0 through F=5.
hints: নিজের কাছে শূন্য এজের পথের দূরত্ব শূন্য।

practice.title: Allow B, then D, then E by hand
practice.statementHtml: Fill Floyd-Warshall graph 0 by intermediate phases A through F. List changed entries in each phase and recover the A-to-F route using next hops.
hints: নতুন পথের প্রথম ধাপ হবে i থেকে k পথে প্রথম নোডটা।
practice.answerHtml:
There is no useful update through A in the shared DAG because no arc enters A. Allowing B connects A to D at cost 9. Allowing C adds routes into E. Allowing D improves B to E, and allowing E improves routes into F.

Allowed new intermediateStrictly improved pairs and new distances
Anone
BA->D=9
CA->E=10; B->E=9
DA->F=15; B->E=7; B->F=11
EA->F=13; B->F=10; C->F=11; D->F=5
Fnone

The final row for A is 0,4,2,9,10,13. These differ from the undirected Dijkstra distances because Floyd-Warshall follows the selected directed arcs. In particular, A cannot use C to B because only B to C exists. Comparing algorithms requires comparing graph direction as well as weights.

The animation shows the full matrix and the current allowed intermediate k. It highlights the two subpath cells before a finite candidate comparison. INF pairs are skipped because no joined route exists. A successful update changes one matrix cell and the hidden next-hop information together.

The recovered next hops for A to F are next[A][F]=C, next[C][F]=E and next[E][F]=F. Their edge weights are 2,8,3, giving the final cost 13.

practice.title: Partition routes by their newest allowed intermediate by hand
practice.statementHtml: Derive the Floyd-Warshall intermediate-set recurrence. Prove the outer-k phase invariant and explain the in-place update assumption and first-hop reconstruction rule.
hints: নতুন পথের প্রথম ধাপ হবে i থেকে k পথে প্রথম নোডটা।
practice.answerHtml:
Assume the table before outer iteration k contains shortest costs with only earlier intermediates. An optimal route with the enlarged allowed set either omits k or contains k. If it omits k, the existing entry already covers it. If it contains k, choose a shortest simple representative and split it at k.

The two subpaths use only previously allowed intermediate vertices, so their best costs are already available. Taking the smaller candidate yields an attainable route no more expensive than any valid route. This proves the recurrence by induction from the direct-edge base.

Why can the two-dimensional table be updated in place? Without negative cycles, dist[k][k] is zero. During iteration k, routes from i to k and from k to j cannot strictly improve merely by adding a zero-length visit through k. Those boundary entries remain stable, so candidate subpaths retain the meanings needed throughout the iteration.

Interchanging i and j inside a fixed k iteration is safe. Moving k inward breaks the phase invariant because some cells may consume paths with intermediates that other cells have not yet allowed. Certain graphs still produce correct answers under an incorrect loop order; that accidental success is not a proof.

practice.title: Derive Floyd-Warshall Algorithm resource bounds
practice.statementHtml: Count all intermediate/source/destination triples. Explain why in-place evaluation and next-hop reconstruction need quadratic tables rather than one matrix per phase.
hints: Count repeated scans separately from the one-time initialisation.
practice.answerHtml:
The outer loop takes V choices of k. Each phase visits V possible sources and V possible destinations. That is exactly V³ candidate positions, so the time is Theta(V³), even when most routes are absent. Finite guards reduce arithmetic work inside a position but do not skip the loops themselves.

The distance and next-hop tables each store V² entries. Their combined space is Theta(V²); the temporary loop variables need constant additional memory. If you retained a separate matrix for every k phase, space would grow to Theta(V³), which is unnecessary when in-place updates satisfy the phase invariant.

Recovering one finite route takes O(L) time for L printed vertices, at most O(V) for a simple route. Printing the entire matrix costs Theta(V²). Those output costs fit below the cubic computation but still matter when comparing an all-pairs table with a single-source query.

quiz.prompt: What does outer iteration k newly permit?
options: Only routes that start at k
Only routes that end at k
Only one edge in the entire matrix
quiz.explanation: Endpoints are unrestricted; the phase controls internal route vertices.

quiz.prompt: Which loop must remain outermost in the usual in-place recurrence?
options: Any loop order is equally valid
quiz.explanation: A full phase must share one allowed-intermediate set.

quiz.prompt: How is next[i][j] updated when a cheaper route uses k?
quiz.explanation: The first hop toward k is the first hop of the new full route.

quiz.prompt: What should dist[i][i] be initially without a negative self-loop?
quiz.explanation: The empty route reaches the same vertex at zero cost.

quiz.prompt: Which diagonal result reveals a negative cycle?
quiz.explanation: A negative closed walk contains a negative cycle.

quiz.prompt: What is the auxiliary table space of Floyd-Warshall with next hops?
quiz.explanation: Two V-by-V tables have the same quadratic order.

quiz.prompt: When does a negative cycle make an ordered pair i,j unbounded below?
options: i can reach the cycle and the cycle can reach j
Only when the direct edge i to j is negative
quiz.explanation: Both reachability directions are required to use the cycle on that route.

quiz.prompt: What final all-pairs distance replaces the direct 0-to-2 cost nine?
quiz.explanation: Going through vertex 1 costs two plus three, which is five.

quiz.prompt: Which first hop is saved when 0-to-2 improves through vertex 1?
quiz.explanation: The first hop of the joined route is next[0][1], namely one.

quiz.prompt: What unreachable marker survives for the reverse 2-to-0 direction?
quiz.explanation: No directed path returns to vertex 0, so the guarded update leaves 999.

quiz.prompt: Why can in-place Floyd updates use the same k row and column within a phase without negative cycles?
options: The algorithm never reads its own table
The zero k diagonal prevents strict improvements of those boundary entries
The endpoints must differ from k
quiz.explanation: Distances into and out of k retain the previous-phase values needed by the recurrence.
